700587.t: From Proto-Hellenic *akouhō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ḱh₂owsyéti, and cognate with English hear, hark and harken. In this word, the diphthong ου (ou) is genuine (see spurious diphthong on Wikipedia for an explanation).

700508.t: From ἀ- (a-, privative alpha) + καθαίρω (kathaírō, “to cleanse”) + -τος (-tos).

700504.t: From earlier *αἰϝών (*aiwṓn), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyu- (“vital force, life, long life, eternity”), whence also ἀεί (aeí, “always”). Cognate with Latin aevum, English aye.

700511.t: First found from the Egyptiots Aretaios and Dioskurides, a borrowing from Coptic ⲭⲁⲕⲓ (khaki), ⲕⲁⲕⲉ (kake), ⲕⲉⲕⲉⲓ (kekei, “darkness”) from Egyptian kkw (“darkness”), acknowledging its providing shade in the desert, with a preformative analogical to ἄκανθα…

700560.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂éḱmō. Cognates include Sanskrit अश्म॑न् (áśman), Avestan 𐬀𐬐𐬨𐬀𐬥 (akman), Old English hamor (English hammer), and Lithuanian akmuõ.

700559.t: From Proto-Hellenic *akmā́, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“point, sharp”). Cognates include ἀκή (akḗ, “point”) and ἄκρος (ákros).

700599.t: Uncertain According to Beekes, probably of Pre-Greek origin. He is sceptical of a connection with either κρίζω (krízō, “to creak”) or Cretan ἄχηρον (ákhēron, “grasshopper”).

700517.t: Etymology tree Proto-Hellenic *akā́ Ancient Greek ἀκή (akḗ) Proto-Indo-European *h₂endʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *h₂éndʰos Proto-Hellenic *ántʰos Ancient Greek ἄνθος (ánthos) Pre-Greek? Ancient Greek ἄκανθα Traditionally derived from…

700561.t: From ἀκούω (akoúō, “to hear”) + -η (-ē, verbal noun suffix).

700568.t: A double-ablauted formation from κέλευθος (kéleuthos, “path”) + copulative ἀ- (a-).

700597.t: Disputed. Commonly held to be formed from ἄκρος (ákros, “sharp”) and another element of uncertain provenance, e.g. εἴβω (eíbō, “to drop, let fall”) according to Schwyzer, though this is rejected by Beekes & van Beek.

700544.t: Often cited as borrowed from Iranian, compared to Sogdian 𐼸𐼷𐼻𐼰𐼸 (kynʾk /⁠kīnak, kēnak⁠/, “sword”), though this etymology is disputed.

700596.t: From ἀκριβής (akrībḗs) + -ια (-ia). Synchronically analyzable as ἀκριβής (akrībḗs) + -εια (-eia).

700552.t: From ἀ- (ă-, not; without) + κλέω (kléō, “to make famous”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix).

700534.t: ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + κατεργάζομαι (katergázomai, “to effect by labor, achieve”) + -τος (-tos, “adjectival suffix”).

700532.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + καθίστημι (kathístēmi, “to set in order”) + -τος (-tos).
